newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends higher on inflows.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends higher on inflows.

text.p: The Philippine peso continued its upward trek on Tuesday as inflows increased on the back of Standard & Poor's raising the country's sovereign rating by one notch.

The peso closed at 26.336 against the dollar from 26.340 on a surge of inflows for direct and portfolio investments, traders said. The day's average was at 26.336 from 26.338. Volume was lower at $192.50 million from $207 million.
"I believe these were mostly capital-intensive investments," a trader said, referring to the nature of the inflows.
Traders said the Central Bank had to intervene in the market to curb the peso's strength.
A foreign bank dealer estimated the Central Bank purchased about $80 milllion at 26.335 and 26.336.
Another trader predicted the peso is not likely to rise beyond 26.335 for now. "We have a large trade deficit. The Central Bank wants the dollar a little higher," he said.
